'''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|qid=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|qid=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|qid=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}:
* {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchija_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1502690}}
* {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|斎主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikotoja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1107286}}
* {{ill|Amenokoyane no Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenokoyane no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyaneqid=Q2564508}}
* {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|qid=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Kami|1=Himegami}}

== History ==
The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrineja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-daja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|qid=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|qid=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōjicomment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>

During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq=Gō-sha|qq=}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

== History ==
The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manorja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.

Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

The shrine enshrines the following four {{ill|Column|en|Column|qid=Q4817|lt=Kami|1=Column}} (deities), identical to those of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|qid=Q714559|lt=Kasuga-taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}:

== History ==
The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrineja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-daja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|qid=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|qid=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōjicomment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>

During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq=Gō-sha|qq=}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

== History ==
The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manorja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.

Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.

'''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}, [[Tokushima (city)|Tokushima City]], [[Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima Prefecture]], Japan. It is situated at the eastern foot of Mount Ōtakiyama within Bizan.

== Enshrined Deities ==
The shrine venerates the {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|fr|Kasuga_no_Kami|ja|春日神|1=Kasuga-no-Kami|2=ja|3=春日神|4=fr|5=Kasuga no Kami|6=zh|7=春日權現|8=wuu|9=春日權現|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-no-Kami|qq=}} just like that of [[Kasuga-taisha]]

== History ==
The shrine traces its origins to a Kasuga Shrine originally enshrined in {{ill|Tomida Manor|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomida Manorja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} of [[Yamato Province]] (present-day {{ill|Iritamura|ja|入田村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iritamura|qq=}} in [[Tokushima City|Tokushima City]]). During the invasion of [[Awa Province]] by [[Hachisuka Iemasa]], the shrine was relocated to its current location at Ōtakiyama 1 in {{ill|Bizan Town|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Town|qq=}}. This history is documented in the *Awa-shi* from 1815 (Bunka 12). Another theory suggests that in 1586 (Tenshō 14), during the construction of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokushima_Castle Tokushima Castle], the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiyamura|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiyamura|qq=}} to serve as the castle's tutelary shrine.

Under the governance of the [[Hachisuka clan]], the shrine, known as "Kasuga Daimyōjin," gained significant reverence, receiving annual offerings of 10 koku of rice. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine's name was officially changed to Kasuga Shrine, and it was designated a Prefectural Shrine. The site includes the spring known as *Kasuga Water*, part of the {{ill|Bizan Springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bizan Springs|qq=}}.
